faq.question: What is the difference between Form 26AS and AIS?
faq.answer: Form 26AS is a tax credit statement: since assessment year 2023-24 it shows only TDS and TCS against your PAN. AIS is much broader. It includes that TDS plus interest, dividends, securities and mutual fund transactions, large financial transactions, taxes paid and refunds. Use 26AS to check your TDS credits, and AIS to check that every income is in your return.

faq.question: What is TIS in AIS?
faq.answer: TIS (Taxpayer Information Summary) is a category-wise summary of your AIS. It shows the value the system processed and the value after your feedback or the source's confirmation. That second figure is what pre-fills your income tax return, which is why giving feedback on wrong AIS entries before filing is useful.

faq.question: Should I report income exactly as AIS shows it?
faq.answer: Report the correct income. Where AIS is right, include it. Where AIS is wrong (a duplicate, another person's transaction, a sale shown instead of the gain), give feedback in AIS and report the correct figure in your return. Don't copy AIS blindly, and don't ignore it either.

faq.question: Why is TDS in my Form 16 more than in 26AS?
faq.answer: Usually because your employer deducted the TDS but filed its TDS return late or with an error, so it hasn't reached your PAN in 26AS. Ask the employer to correct its TDS return. Claim only what 26AS shows; once the correction appears, you can revise your return to claim the rest.

faq.question: Will I still get Form 16 next year?
faq.answer: For salary earned up to March 2026, yes, by 15 June 2026. For salary earned from April 2026, employers issue Form 130 instead, under the new Income-tax Rules. It serves the same purpose with a slightly different layout.
